core_obligations: Assume f locally of finite type over a locally Noetherian Y and choose the source-and-target presentation with h locally of finite type (proof lines 5802-5805).
Apply the scheme case to h to get that h is locally of finite presentation (proof lines 5805-5808).
Conclude that f is locally of finite presentation by definition (proof lines 5808-5809).
Derive part (2) from part (1) since finite type and quasi-separated imply quasi-compact and quasi-separated (proof lines 5811-5812).
difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma with two assertions: over a locally Noetherian base a locally of finite type morphism is locally of finite presentation, and a morphism of finite type and quasi-separated is of finite presentation (source lines 5789-5799). The proof of (1) uses the source-and-target presentation of local finite typeness, reduces to a morphism of schemes h that is locally of finite type over a locally Noetherian base, applies the scheme case to get local finite presentation of h, and reads the property back for f by definition; part (2) follows because finite type plus quasi-separated means quasi-compact and quasi-separated.
